Indian Immunologicals managing director K. Anand Kumar speaks at the FABA award ceremony. | Photo Credit: Arrangement
The Federation of Asian Biotech Associations (FABA) has presented the FABA Lifetime Achievement Award to K. Anand Kumar, managing director of Indian Immunologicals (IIL).
He was awarded for his contributions to biotechnology, vaccine research, development and manufacturing, and the advancement of India’s human and animal healthcare sectors. It recognises Mr. Anand Kumar’s work to strengthen India’s vaccine ecosystem and making quality vaccines accessible and affordable, IIL said in a release on Friday.
Previous recipients include Serum Institute of India CMD Cyrus Poonawalla; former president of R&D at GlaxoSmithKline, Patrick Vallance, former director general of ICMR Balram Bhargava and former chief scientist of the World Health Organization Soumya Swaminathan.
“Deeply honoured to receive the award and consider the recognition a tribute to the collective efforts of the scientific community, researchers, healthcare professionals and the entire team at Indian Immunologicals,” Mr. Anand Kumar said.
